geometry: Dense 3D LBM (index-3d.html), N^3 lattice. Two analytic gates and one reporting scenario -- see d3-scenarios.mjs's header for why these two and not the 3D Taylor-Green vortex at Re=1600 that plans/3D.md M1 originally named.

gates.duct: Square-duct Poiseuille flow: periodic in x, stationary no-slip walls on y and z, uniform Guo body force sized to a target peak velocity. Started from REST, so the initial condition is independent of the reference solution -- this gate cannot be passed by a shared mistake between the seed and the check. Scored on the steady u_x cross-section (averaged along x) against the classical series solution. `x_spread_tol` bounds the variation of u_x ALONG the periodic axis relative to the peak: a settled duct flow is x-invariant by construction, so a nonzero spread means either an unconverged run or something wrong with the periodic direction, and it is checked separately from the profile error rather than being allowed to hide inside it.
gates.beltrami: Decaying ABC (Beltrami) flow, triply periodic. curl(u) = k*u, so the nonlinear term is a pure gradient and u(t) = u0 * exp(-nu k^2 t) EXACTLY, with the spatial shape preserved. Genuinely three-dimensional and time-dependent -- an asymmetry between the axes (a transposed index, a dropped uz term in feq, a wrong ez entry) breaks shape preservation, which is what field_l2_tol measures, while decay_rate_tol measures the viscosity the solver actually realizes.
gates.tgv: 3D Taylor-Green vortex. NOT a gate: the nonlinear term does not vanish, so there is no closed form, and the standard Re=1600 comparison is against digitized DNS dissipation curves at 256^3-512^3 that this project does not have. Present as the initial condition that comparison will need, and reported (kinetic energy, enstrophy, dissipation rate) so a regression in it is at least VISIBLE. Reported cases have no tolerances and never fail the suite.
gates.sphere: Flow past a PINNED sphere in uniform crossflow, ALBC sponge on every face, Cd = Fx / (1/2 rho U^2 pi R^2) against the Schiller-Naumann correlation Cd = 24/Re (1 + 0.15 Re^0.687). Below Re ~ 210 the wake is steady and axisymmetric, so unlike the 2D cylinder there is nothing to time-average -- Cd simply settles, which `settle_tol` verifies rather than assumes (two samples, 70% and 100% of the run). `lateral_tol` bounds the cross-flow force |(Cl, Cs)| / Cd: it must vanish by symmetry, and it is an INDEPENDENT check -- a transposed axis or a wrong torque in the six-scalar force reduction shows up there and not in Cd at all. Cases come in resolution pairs at the same Re so the suite can assert that refining moves Cd TOWARD the reference; a single tolerance can be met by a body of the wrong size with a compensating error, a convergence trend cannot.
gates.spin: The 6-DOF integrator with the fluid force switched off (NO_FLUID_FORCE), compared step for step against d3-body.mjs's stepFreeBody(). Not a fluid case: shaders/d3_physics.wgsl is the hardest new code in M2 and its errors are the least visible -- a wrong gyroscopic coupling still conserves |L| exactly and simply tumbles wrongly -- so it is checked against the host reference on real GPU code. The spin starts near the INTERMEDIATE principal axis so the compared trajectory is the tumbling one; `movedCheck` asserts the body actually turned, since agreement on a body that barely moved would prove nothing.
gates.amr: AMR at N=2 (plans/3D.md M3), scored on the SAME analytic Beltrami flow as the dense gate. `refine=all` refines every block, so there is no coarse/fine interface anywhere: it validates the octree pool, the fine solver with DIRECT_GHOST, the ring, the coarse->fine interpolation, the fine->coarse restriction and the S_Advance schedule end to end, against an exact solution. It should be BETTER than the dense run of the same case, not merely equal -- the fine level resolves the mode at twice the resolution -- and it is: decay-rate error -1.22e-4 against dense's +9.38e-4. The RB=4 and RB=8 cases are bit-identical to each other, which is the evidence that the tile decomposition does not affect the answer. NOT GATED HERE: a partially-refined domain. See amr_interface_note.

measurement.duct_steps: settle_multiple x the (1,1) duct mode's time constant 2a^2/(nu pi^2), rounded per case at run time, so the same physical settling is used regardless of N or nu
measurement.beltrami_checkpoints: multiples of td = 1/(nu k^2), k = 2 pi / N
measurement.decay_rate: fit via -ln(rms(t_b)/rms(t_a))/(t_b - t_a) between the last two checkpoints, rms taken over the strided full-volume sample
measurement.sphere_steps: settle_convective x the convective time D/U, rounded per case. Cd was observed settled to three digits by ~20 D/U at every Re tested; the default 30 leaves margin.
measurement.sphere_cd: Cd = Fx / (1/2 rho U^2 A), A = pi R^2, rho = 1 in lattice units. Fx is read back through the body state, which d3_physics.wgsl fills every step INCLUDING for a pinned body.
measurement.amr_checkpoints: multiples of the Beltrami decay time td, as for the dense case, so the AMR and dense numbers are directly comparable

tolerances_note: Set from measurement, 2026-09-09, RTX 4080. Observed duct L2rel spans 6.3e-5 (Q27, tau=0.933) to 1.7e-3 (tau=0.6); observed beltrami worst-checkpoint L2rel spans 9.4e-5 to 8.3e-3 and decay-rate relative error 1.2e-5 to 2.1e-3, converging at second order in N (2.08e-3 -> 9.38e-4 -> 5.60e-4 for N = 32, 48, 64), which is the expected O(k^2) lattice-viscosity correction. Tolerances sit a few times above the worst observed value: loose enough not to be a resolution-dependent tripwire, far tighter than any real defect. tau=0.9330127 is (1/2) + sqrt(3)/4, the BGK value at which the TRT magic parameter Lambda = (tau-1/2)^2 equals 3/16 and halfway bounce-back places the wall EXACTLY halfway between the last fluid cell and the first solid one -- which is the convention d3-scenarios.mjs's ductCoord() and shaders/common_d3_step.wgsl both assume. The tau=0.8 and tau=0.6 duct cases are deliberately off that value and are there to keep the wall-position error visible rather than tuned away.
sphere_tolerances_note: Measured 2026-09-09, RTX 4080. BOUNCE-BACK is the gating coupling and lands +6.9% to +12.8% above Schiller-Naumann across Re = 20..200 at D = 16, falling with resolution (Re=20: 2.944 at D=16, 2.907 at D=24, against 2.610). That offset is expected and well documented for a staircased bounce-back sphere at these resolutions -- the discrete surface has more area than the smooth one and the effective diameter exceeds the nominal -- plus ~1.2% blockage. cd_tol_rel of 0.15 covers it with margin while remaining far tighter than any real defect. THE DIFFUSE (chi) CASES ARE REGRESSION CHECKS, NOT PHYSICS CHECKS, and are scored against RECORDED values rather than against literature: measured Cd 4.649 (Re=20, D=16), 3.878 (Re=20, D=24), 2.523 (Re=100, D=16) against references 2.610 / 2.610 / 1.092. That is the SAME open diffuse-interface-width issue CLAUDE.md already records for the 2D dense-reference cylinder (Cd 1.950 against 1.35+-0.15), and for the same reason: the chi band is a fixed number of cells wide regardless of resolution, so the effective body radius exceeds the nominal one and Cd converges FROM ABOVE (4.649 -> 3.878 as D goes 16 -> 24). It is worse in 3D than in 2D because the frontal area error goes as (1 + d/R)^2 rather than (1 + d/R). Do NOT re-baseline these against Schiller-Naumann; treat a change in them as a regression to explain.
amr_interface_note: The coarse/fine interface had TWO defects. One is FIXED (2026-09-09): the grid transfers applied the PRE-collision Dupuis-Chopard fneq factor (tau_f/tau_c)*dx_f/dx_c to POST-collision populations. This solver's step kernels are fused pull-stream+collide, so every buffer holds f AFTER collision, and the factor that applies is (tau_f-1)/(tau_c-1)/2 -- at tau=0.8 that is -0.25 against the +0.6875 the code used, wrong magnitude and opposite SIGN. It was found by measuring mass and momentum separately (tools/analyze-d3-interface.js): mass sat at the f32 readback floor while momentum leaked seven orders above its own floor, linearly in t. That asymmetry IS the diagnosis -- fneq has no zeroth or first moment so it cannot touch a mass flux, but the second moment is the viscous stress, i.e. the momentum flux. The amr-all cases could not see it (they are bit-identical across the fix: with every block refined the rescaled coarse f is discarded and the rings are never read), which is why amr-box-RB4 is now in this file. STILL OPEN: the interface is not CONSERVATIVE. With the rescale correct a partially-refined run still converges at FIRST order -- whole-domain L2rel at t=0.5*td is 1.36e-2 / 9.02e-3 / 7.04e-3 at N=32/48/64 (ratios 1.51, 1.28 against first order's 1.5, 1.33), while the no-interface controls sit at 4.6e-3 / 2.3e-3 / 2.0e-3. That is the classic composite-grid signature: the two sides compute the seam flux independently and disagree. The fix is refluxing and it is the first item of M4 (plans/3D.md M3 sketches the shape). Until it lands a partially-refined 3D run is not trustworthy for a quantitative number, and the sphere-with-AMR comparison against M2's dense Cd is deliberately NOT part of this suite -- it would report the seam, not the solver. M4 UPDATE 2026-09-09: the flux correction (?reflux=1) is built and makes conservation EXACT -- the momentum leak stops dead -- and on a corner-free seam (?refine=slab) halves the field error. It is OPT-IN and not the default because on a seam with a convex corner it is far worse than leaving it off: the fine lattice's diagonal channels carry half what the coarse one does across a corner (D3Q19 has no (1,1,+-1)), so a cell-by-cell flux balance is ill-posed there. amr-box-RB4's numbers below are with reflux OFF, which is the default. M4.1b UPDATE 2026-09-09: refluxing is SUPERSEDED by Chen et al. 2006's explode/coalesce (?interface=explode), which as of the coalesce orphan pass is exactly conservative in mass AND momentum on every rung of the geometry ladder (all/slab/bar/box) -- box mass drift -2.69e+1 -> -5.85e-3 at t=8, momentum frozen rather than growing. THAT PATH IS NOT THE DEFAULT AND HAS NO CASE IN THIS FILE: every number here, amr-box-RB4 included, is still the ?interface=interp path and is unchanged by it (verified bit-identical). Explode gets its own cases in M4.1d, after the linear explosion lands. See plans/3D.md M4.1b.
amr_box_note: REGRESSION BOUNDS, NOT PHYSICS TOLERANCES -- the same distinction sphere_diffuse_cases carries. This case has a real coarse/fine interface and the interface is still first-order (see amr_interface_note), so its error is dominated by a known defect and there is nothing to score it against except its own measured value. The tolerances are ~30% above what was measured on an RTX 4080 on 2026-09-09, which is tight enough to catch a factor-of-two regression and loose enough not to fire on driver noise. The point of the case is that BEFORE it existed nothing in this suite ever loaded a partially-refined 3D run, which is exactly how the pre/post-collision rescale bug survived M3. When refluxing lands these numbers should FALL and must be re-baselined, not widened. Checkpoints are deliberately short (0.25 and 0.5 decay times): the seam error spreads over the whole domain by 3 t_d, and a saturated field measures the pollution rather than the injection. Measured 2026-09-09, RTX 4080: field L2rel 9.012e-3 and decay-rate rel err 1.024e-2. The SAME case run with ?dcpre=1 -- the pre-collision factor, i.e. the bug -- gives 4.618e-2, so this case would have failed its own bound by 3.8x before the fix. That is what makes it a real guard rather than a recorded curiosity.
